title: git push
definition: Uploads local repository content (commits and branches) to a remote repository.
simpleExplanation: The upload button. You finished your feature, you made your commits locally, but your boss can't see them yet. `git push` takes your local timeline and sends it up to GitHub for everyone to see.
realWorldExample: You finish your work for the day, commit it, and run `git push origin main` so the server has a backup in case your laptop breaks overnight.
useCases: Backing up code to the cloud

basic: If you edit a file, can you just run `git push` immediately to save it to GitHub?
intermediate: What does the `-u` flag do in `git push -u origin main`?

answers.question: Push immediately?
answers.answer: No. `git push` ONLY uploads COMMITS. You must `git add` and `git commit` your changes first. Uncommitted changes are completely ignored by `git push`.

answers.question: What is the -u flag?
answers.answer: It stands for 'set-upstream'. It links your local branch to the remote branch permanently. After using `-u` once, you can just type `git push` in the future instead of typing out `git push origin main` every time.

codeExample:
# 1. Save your work locally FIRST
$ git commit -am "Finish the homepage"

# 2. Upload that commit to the 'origin' server, on the 'main' branch
$ git push origin main

# 3. Create a brand new branch, and push it to the server for the first time
# (-u sets the upstream link so Git remembers where to push next time)
$ git checkout -b my-new-feature
$ git push -u origin my-new-feature

# 4. In the future, you can just type:
$ git push
